newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac says disapproves of Renault method.
newsitem.headline: Chirac says disapproves of Renault method.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac said on Monday he did not approve of the way in which French carmaker Renault had behaved in its recent decision to close a car factory in Belgium.

"I believe there has to be a minimum of form and this must be respected," Chirac said in a television interview. Asked whether that meant he disapproved of Renault's recent actions, he said, "I do not approve."
Renault said on February 27 it planned to close its Vilvoorde plant in Belgium with the loss of 3,100 jobs, and later said it planned to cut 2,764 jobs in France in 1997, double the number in 1996.
The company has drawn fire from unions and French and Belgian politicians who say they are appalled by the brutality of the measures and the short notice.

Chirac also said companies had a responsibility to society in the way they treated workers. They had to recognise that by simply going after profits in the short term they may fail to take account of the cost to society of unemployment. This cost would eventually have to be paid for, very possibly by companies themselves.
